requirements.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:23 passes a validated mention into formatContent; :43-49 no mention when null, otherwise appends "\n<@{$mentionId}>" on its own line and truncates the base to MaxContentLength - mb_strlen($suffix) so the total stays <=1800 and the mention survives; :59-77 mentionId() trims and accepts only /^[0-9]{17,20}$/ (rejecting @everyone, @here, abc, 123, embedded newlines), also accepting is_int; config/services.php:39 and .env.example:10 add services.discord.mention_id from DISCORD_MENTION_ID (contract key/env kept); docs/ops/devops.md:102,110 and docs/ops/logging.md:122 document the env var; send() signature and the webhook no-op/soft-fail paths are untouched.

conventions.evidence: Matches sibling style in app/Ops (private helper with PHPDoc, same mb_* usage) and keeps docs in sync (docs/ops/devops.md:102,110; docs/ops/logging.md:122). Deviations: no Pest test added anywhere in the diff, contradicting conventions.md:15-18 ('No production code without a test; everything implemented ships with a test') and the Laravel test-first rule; CHANGELOG.md is not updated with an [Unreleased] entry as required by conventions.md:103.

security.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:71-77 whitelists 17-20 ASCII digits after trim before building the mention, so a misconfigured value cannot inject @everyone/@here or break the message; the id is the only new input and it is never logged or echoed to a view; existing redaction via safe() (:80-88 region) and the soft-fail logging that avoids leaking the webhook URL (:26+) are unchanged.

tests.evidence: change.diff contains only .env.example, app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php, config/services.php, docs/ops/devops.md and docs/ops/logging.md (diff --git lines 1,14,81,93,114); no tests/ file is added or modified, so the mention formatting, the 17-20 digit validation edge cases and the truncation-with-mention path are entirely untested.

simplicity.evidence: One small private helper (mentionId(), :59-77) plus a single extra parameter threaded into the existing formatContent (:32) and one config line (config/services.php:39); no new classes, services or duplicated formatting logic, and the 1800-char logic is reused rather than reimplemented.

readability.evidence: Clear names (mentionId, $candidate, $suffix), a focused PHPDoc explaining why validation exists (:52-58), early returns for the invalid cases (:67-75) and a two-branch return in formatContent (:43-49); consistent with the surrounding file's style, no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: All five touched files serve the task: the config key, env example, the alert class and the two ops docs named in requirement 6; no unrelated refactors, no UI/Livewire changes, no allowed_mentions or role-mention work (explicitly out of scope in task.md:48-51).

issues.explanation: The project requires a test for every feature, but the change ships none, so the mention formatting, the snowflake validation (including '@everyone', '123', embedded newlines), the truncation-with-mention case and the unchanged no-mention/no-webhook behavior are all unverified.
conventions.md:103 requires an [Unreleased] CHANGELOG entry when behavior or docs change, and this change does not add one.

review.summary: The change adds an optional DISCORD_MENTION_ID setting, validates it as a 17-20 digit snowflake and appends '<@ID>' on its own line, reserving room so the mention survives the 1800-character truncation; config and the two ops docs are updated consistently. The implementation looks correct and safe, but no Pest/PHPUnit tests are added and the CHANGELOG is not updated, so it needs changes (tests at minimum) before merging.
